_law: WS06 (audit 2026-11-05 item 6): research answers may only RELEASE after a server-enforced action/citation/claim check — in TypeScript (lib/chat/answer-release.ts, wired by lib/chat/web-tool-loop.ts) and in Rust (crates/ruke-server/src/chat/answer_release.rs, wired by chat/web_loop.rs). This matrix is the ONE truth for the repair semantics: both sides read these exact bytes (vitest reads this file; Rust include_str!'s it). No brand/site rules — inputs are generic. MHR-D (brief 2026-11-05): the mhrD section byte-locks the NON-DESTRUCTIVE diagnosis (same detectors as the audit, reporting only) and the exact harness-feedback message injected into the existing tool loop when an answer is held back — the MODEL then decides the next action (retrieve / re-attach citations / state the gap). The destructive `cases` above stay in force until MHR-F evolves them; D is deliberately a half-state.

mhrD._law: MHR-D (brief 2026-11-05): the SAME detectors run NON-DESTRUCTIVELY first — diagnoseResearchAnswer reports the actual harness state (fabricated [S#] markers, sentences whose volatile/mis-cited claims resolve to NO minted source, research wording on a zero-retrieval turn) without rewriting a byte. When the loop holds such an answer back, the harness injects ONE feedback message into the EXISTING tool loop (this matrix byte-locks it) and the MODEL decides the next action: retrieve more, re-attach citations, or state the gap. One feedback per turn; the model then continues with tools still armed — no second research engine. Feedback triggers whenever any diagnosis field is non-empty.
